judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic claims are exact. Beaker plot stacks 1,1,4,1,1 give 8 beakers (p4); the eighths sum 1/8+1/4+4*(3/8)+1/2+5/8 = 24/8 = 3 cups (p5) and the equal share is 3/8 cup (p6); mode 3/8 (p2); 4 - 1 = 3 (p3). Leaf plot stacks 1,2,4,2,1 give range 5/4 - 1/4 = 1 in (p8), 2+1 = 3 leaves longer than 3/4 in (p9), 30 quarters = 7 1/2 in (p10), mean 3/4 in (p11), and 12(a) = 2 leaves at 1/2 in. Where I part company is 'The manual explanation correctly interprets a repeated fractional measurement.' The manual entry does not describe the printed problem at all. verify.json id 12's manual desc is about a student named Priya who wants to redraw the leaf plot using only the lengths that occurred, and it grades the scale-spacing argument. The worksheet's 12(b) asks something else entirely: 'Write one or two sentences saying which part of the plot answers each of the two questions above, and why counting X's can never answer the second one.' The word 'Priya' appears nowhere in worksheet.tex or worksheet.pdf. The answer key follows the printed question correctly, so the human reviewer is handed a grading rubric for a problem that was never asked. The judge reported reviewing one manual item and did not notice the two disagree.

strengths_to_preserve: The sheet deliberately changes scale halfway: the beaker plot is marked in eighths and the leaf plot in quarters, and the key names the trap explicitly ('the same physical distance along the line now means twice as much length ... children who do not check the scale read the second plot with the first plot's ruler'). That is the 5.MD.B.2 skill rather than fraction arithmetic wearing a plot as decoration.

The how-many / how-much distinction is the spine of the whole set and the traps enforce it numerically: problem 5 declares 8 (counted X's instead of adding amounts) and problem 10 declares 10 (counted leaves instead of adding lengths), both machine-proved to differ from the true 3 cups and 15/2 in. The key's diagnostic -- 'ask the child whether their answer counts beakers or measures water' -- turns a wrong number into a diagnosis.

Problem 9 tests strict inequality on a plot: the four X's sitting ON 3/4 in are excluded, and the key says why ('ask them whether a leaf can be longer than itself'). Off-by-one on the boundary mark is the most common line-plot error and it is targeted on purpose.

root_causes.description: A `manual` entry's free-text desc is the only instruction the human grader receives, and nothing binds it to the printed problem. Here it describes a different problem from an earlier draft, and every gate still passes because the gates read structure (ids, counts, units), never the semantics of the desc.
evidence: verify.json id 12 manual desc: 'Priya wants to redraw the leaf plot with only the lengths that actually occurred ... The child must explain what the scale on a line plot has to promise'
worksheet.pdf p5 problem 12(b): 'Write one or two sentences saying which part of the plot answers each of the two questions above, and why counting X's can never answer the second one.'
'Priya' does not occur anywhere in worksheet.tex, worksheet.pdf or answer_key.pdf
answer_key.pdf p4 12(b) marking guide grades the PRINTED question (lengths read from the bottom, totals need the fractions added), so the key and the verification data disagree about what was asked
gate_log.txt reports all gates green including verify-ws and answer-key-ak

root_causes.description: Per-id coverage again leaves printed blanks unchecked, including two that are final answers in their own right rather than scaffolding.
evidence: Problem 7 asks two questions -- 'How many leaves were 3/4 inch long?' and 'How many leaves were exactly one inch long?' -- and verify.json id 7 holds a single read_data entry (3/4 -> 4); the key answers 'Two leaves were exactly one inch long'
Problem 8 prints 'Longest leaf: __  Shortest leaf: __' before the difference; verify.json id 8 checks only the range 1
Problem 5 prints 'Rewrite 1/4 as __ eighths and 1/2 as __ eighths'; only the 3-cup total is checked
Problem 10 prints 'Quarters altogether: __' (30) and problems 6 and 11 print 'Total / number: __ / __', none of them checked

improvements.title: Bind every manual entry's desc to the text of the problem it grades
improvements.proposed_change: Add a binding check for `manual` entries to tests/check_answer_key.py (or a sibling checker run in the same gate): for each manual entry, segment the worksheet .tex, take the desc's distinctive tokens -- capitalised names, numerals and fraction literals -- and require that the named entities appear in the segment for that id. A desc naming a person, an object or a quantity that the printed problem never mentions is a hard failure with both texts echoed. The rule is cheap because it only asks whether the desc talks about the same objects, not whether it grades correctly.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_answer_key_binding.py gains this case verbatim: a worksheet segment for problem 12 that asks 'which part of the plot answers each of the two questions' and a verify.json manual desc naming 'Priya' and a redrawn scale. Assert the checker exits non-zero and prints both strings; then replace the desc with one that names the printed question and assert exit 0. Every gate passes on this input today, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: A human reviewer is never handed a rubric for a problem that is not on the sheet. It also catches the general case of a problem being rewritten after its verification entry was authored, which no current gate sees because ids, counts and units all still line up.
improvements.risk: Token overlap is a heuristic: a legitimate desc that abstracts away from the story ('the learner must justify the scale') could fail. Scope the rule to proper nouns and numerals, and let a desc that quotes the printed question satisfy it trivially.

improvements.title: Check the second reading in problem 7 and the longest/shortest slots in problem 8
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the sheet-side gate so coverage is counted per printed response slot, not per problem id. tests/check_answer_line.py already segments the worksheet and reads verify.json; have it also count the response slots each segment prints (\ansblank, \answerline, \ansline, and \underline{\hspace{...}}) and fail when a problem prints more slots than its id has verify entries, unless the surplus is explicitly absorbed by a 'manual' entry. SKILL.md's JSON-format section should state the rule as 'one check per printed blank', replacing today's 'at least one check per problem id'.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_unit_binding.py gains a fixture from problem 7: a segment printing both 'How many leaves were 3/4 inch long? \ansblank' and 'How many leaves were exactly one inch long? \ansblank' against a verify.json with one read_data entry for id 7. Assert exit 1 naming the uncovered slot; add read_data (key '1' -> 2) and assert exit 0. No current gate counts slots, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Two printed answers the key already supplies (2 leaves at one inch; longest 1 1/4 in and shortest 1/4 in) gain machine proof, and the same rule covers the eighths rewrites in problem 5 and the quarter total in problem 10.
improvements.risk: Same lexical-counting risk as elsewhere: scaffolding blanks meant as thinking space would be forced into the JSON. Allow an explicit 'scaffold' marker so a deliberate working line does not demand an entry.

case_summary: Twelve line-plot questions across two deliberately different scales, all arithmetic independently recomputed here and correct, with traps that separate counting X's from adding the amounts they stand for and a key that names the diagnosis rather than the answer. The ACCEPT is right and the mathematics is sound. The serious finding is not arithmetic: verify.json's manual entry for problem 12 grades a problem about a student named Priya redrawing the plot's scale, which appears nowhere on the sheet, while the printed 12(b) asks which part of the plot answers which question. The answer key follows the printed version, so the artifacts disagree with the verification data about what was asked, and every gate passed. Secondary: problem 7 prints two questions and verifies one, problem 8 prints longest/shortest slots that go unchecked, and the Quick Answers row for problem 12 prints '2' with no marker that part (b) is a manual item at all.
